name: MB85RC256V 32 KB I2C FRAM
description: Fujitsu 256 Kbit (32 KB) ferroelectric RAM with an I2C interface (up to 1 MHz): non-volatile like EEPROM but every byte writes instantly with no wait and 10^12 write cycles. Runs on 2.7-5.5 V. Sold as: Adafruit I2C Non-Volatile FRAM Breakout - 256Kbit / 32KByte (product 1895, 8-pin: VCC, GND, WP, SCL, SDA, A2, A1, A0), I2C address 0x50 (0x50-0x57 with A2-A0), 10 kΩ pull-ups on SDA/SCL.
eli5: A tiny memory chip that remembers numbers and text even when the power is off, and you can rewrite it as often as you like.

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Supply, 2.7-5.5 V. Use 3.3 V with an ESP32/Pico: the board's SDA/SCL pull-ups go to VCC.

pins.name: WP
pins.description: Write protect: high blocks all writes; internal pull-down, leave open to allow writing

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (10 kΩ pull-up to VCC on the board)

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (10 kΩ pull-up to VCC on the board)

pins.name: A2
pins.description: Address bit 2 (internal pull-down; high adds 4 to 0x50)

pins.name: A1
pins.description: Address bit 1 (internal pull-down; high adds 2 to 0x50)

pins.name: A0
pins.description: Address bit 0 (internal pull-down; high adds 1 to 0x50)

buildNotes: Every transfer starts with two memory-address bytes, high byte first (top bit 0, range 0x0000-0x7FFF); data bytes follow for a write.
To read: write the two address bytes without a STOP, then a repeated START and read; the address auto-increments and wraps from 0x7FFF to 0x0000.
No write delay and no page size: data is stored as each byte is acknowledged.
Leave WP unconnected (internal pull-down) or tie it to GND; if WP is high, writes are silently ignored but reads still work.
A2/A1/A0 are read at power-up: change them only with the power off. Up to 8 boards share one bus at 0x50-0x57.
Power the board from 3.3 V when using an ESP32 or Pico: its 10 kΩ SDA/SCL pull-ups go to VCC, and 5 V on those lines can damage 3.3 V GPIOs.
Fresh chips contain unknown data: write a marker/checksum before trusting stored values.

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from mb85rc256v import MB85RC256V

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
fram = MB85RC256V(i2c)
fram.write(0x7F00, b'Sparkbench')
fram.write_u16(0x0100, 12345)
while True:
    text = fram.read(0x7F00, 10).decode()
    num = fram.read_u16(0x0100)
    print('FRAM read: %s %d' % (text, num))
    time.sleep(1)

test.title: Reads back the text and number it wrote to the FRAM

library.note: Passed the Sparkbench part check in simulation and matched an independent datasheet reading. Not yet tested on real hardware.
